title: dynamic batching: seqlen bucketing and padding-minimization heuristics
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation:
Mixed-length request distributions (chat + assistant + embedding prep) result in high padding overhead when continuously batching by arrival time. This PR implements sequence-length aware dynamic batching heuristics to reduce padding and improve token throughput without impacting latency SLOs.

Summary of changes:
- Add seqlen bucketing module in runtime/serving: maintains a lightweight per-model sequence-length histogram (sliding window) and computes adaptive bucket boundaries. Buckets are bounded (max 8) and updated every 10s by default.
- Continuous batching integration: when forming batches, prefer grouping by nearest bucket; allow short adaptive deferral (configurable per-route latency budget) to wait for same-bucket arrivals.
- Padding-minimization strategy: choose bucket boundary and kernel mapping that minimizes expected padding tokens given the recent histogram and kernel alignment constraints.
- KV-cache compatibility: ensure KV cache layout is preserved when reordering requests into bucketed batches; added KV cache index remapping and fast-path for same-seqlen batches to avoid cache lookups overhead.
- Heuristics & fallbacks: cap max deferral to avoid tail latency regressions, fall back to time-based batching when traffic is low or histogram is too noisy, and expose runtime flags for aggressive/ conservative modes.
- Telemetry: new metrics exposed: seqlen_bucket_count, avg_padding_tokens_saved, bucket_deferral_ms, bucket_hit_rate. Added dashboards and alerts for unexpected regressions.
- Tests & benchmarks: unit tests for histogram, end-to-end integration tests for batching correctness, and bench harness updates measuring throughput/latency across mixed-length workloads.

Design notes:
- Bucketing algorithm: use a greedy boundary selection over quantiles of the sliding-window histogram to minimize expected padding subject to a max bucket budget. We evaluate candidate kernel alignment impacts (e.g., 8/16-token GPU-friendly widths) when choosing boundaries.
- Deferral policy: decisions are per-route and per-model. We compute an expected throughput gain from deferring X ms using the recent arrival rate for that bucket. If expected token savings outweigh added latency for p95 targets, allow deferral up to route-configured cap.
- KV cache correctness: to keep cache hits high, we prefer same-seqlen batches for requests that already have cached prefixes. Remapping is O(batch_size) and avoids copying large KV tensors; unit-tested for correctness across split/merge scenarios.

Performance impact (internal benchmarks):
- Mixed conversational workloads (model: redwood-xl, variable seq lengths 8-1024): 12-18% token/sec improvement and 6-10% estimated cost reduction vs baseline continuous batching.
- Tail latency: p50 improved slightly due to lower GPU busy-work; p95 remained within 5% of baseline when deferral caps are set to match existing latency SLOs.
- Low-traffic regimes: algorithm falls back to time-based batching; no measurable regressions.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature flag behind runtime config.
2) Canary: enable on 5% traffic for a single model shard for 24h, validate metrics (avg_padding_tokens_saved > 0, no p95 regressions).
3) Gradual ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 100% over multiple days with automated rollback on alert triggers.

Limitations & future work:
- Current histogram window is uniform; next iteration will add decay weighting for diurnal patterns.
- Kernel-level autotuning could be extended to invite quantized-kernel tradeoffs per bucket.

Related: ENG-1983 (dynamic batching improvements), ENG-2041 (kv-cache stability).

review_comments: Ben Carter: Nice approach. A few asks: 1) add an end-to-end test that simulates shard-level KV cache hits after reordering, 2) make the histogram window configurable via env var, 3) ensure no additional OOM risk when remapping KV tensors.

Ava Martinez: Addressed: added integration test (e13b2f0), expose RDF_SEQLEN_HIST_WINDOW env var (defaults to 10k events), added guardrails to remapping path to avoid extra tensor copies and added unit test for memory safety.
Lina Zhou: Can we add a small benchmark comparing kernel alignment choices (8 vs 16 token widths) and include the results in the PR description?

Ava Martinez: Added kernel alignment evaluation in bench results and summarized in performance impact section. Results show marginally better savings when aligning to 8-token kernels for short sequences on current GPUs; will revisit when we add autotune.
Marco Ruiz: Approved after verifying p95 and GPU utilization graphs on canary run. Left a minor nit about naming in seqlen_bucket.rs.
